title: 4.6 WIND POWER
summary: Wind power converts atmospheric kinetic energy into electricity, and the chapter walks through the physical and locational factors that determine how much a farm produces: siting for consistent, strong wind and sufficient land, the recurring seasonal and daily production patterns, and how site-specific variability and the wake effect between turbines shape actual output. It then turns to the grid-integration consequences of that variability — the need for balancing capacity, fast-start backup to cover sudden regional drop-offs, and transmission constraints when many turbines ramp up together — before closing on the main public concerns, bird mortality and visual impact.
provenance: rewritten orientation from this chapter's concept set; no new claims
